passage_changes.passage: In June 2026, the United States and Iran put their signatures to a memorandum known as the Islamabad MoU. The document is designed to halt open hostilities first, with an immediate ceasefire, and then to open a structured period of talks. Those talks are meant to cover three linked areas: nuclear questions, security in the wider region and relief from sanctions. Movement of commercial vessels through a key maritime route would be restored during this negotiation period, reassuring energy-importing countries. The background to the arrangement is a long dispute. An earlier agreement under which Iran accepted curbs on uranium enrichment and tighter inspections, in return for easing of international economic sanctions, was later abandoned by the United States. Iran responded by gradually reducing its compliance with the terms it had accepted. An international nuclear body, whose work includes promoting peaceful nuclear energy and blocking its military use, plays a central role in verifying any nuclear commitments. The accord also envisions a further comprehensive deal, backed by the United Nations Security Council, once negotiations are complete. Many observers remain cautious about whether the timelines can be met.

Myanmar's President, Min Aung Hlaing, recently completed a five-day official visit to India. It was his first visit since the political transition in Myanmar. The visit came at a time when Myanmar remains central to India's Neighbourhood First Policy, Act East Policy and the wider Indo-Pacific Vision. During the talks, Myanmar gave an assurance on a sensitive security concern. Its territory, it said, would not be used by anti-India insurgent groups operating near the border. Both sides also agreed to promote wider use of the Rupee-Kyat settlement framework, which is already in operation. The two countries reaffirmed their commitment to complete the Kaladan Multi-Modal Transit Transport Project at the earliest. Efforts were also announced to expedite the India-Myanmar-Thailand Trilateral Highway. In education, India increased the number of ICCR scholarships available to Myanmar students. The outcomes cover security, trade settlement, connectivity and people-to-people ties. The talks also reflected the long history between the two neighbours, whose modern boundary was fixed after the Anglo-Burmese War. Trade between the two countries is an important part of the relationship as well.

Narendra Modi has become India's longest continuously serving elected Prime Minister. This milestone was reached after he completed a long run of consecutive days in office, counted from the day he took office in 2014. The record he surpassed was an uninterrupted tenure record held by an earlier Prime Minister. The Prime Minister is the head of the Union Government and the leader of the Council of Ministers. He is normally the leader of the majority party in the Lok Sabha, and the President usually invites that leader to form the government. The Prime Minister is also the chief coordinator of government policy and administration, and he chairs the Union Cabinet. The Prime Minister's salary and allowances are decided by Parliament from time to time. Many Prime Ministers of India have held the office for very different lengths of time, and their careers are often compared through such records. Students preparing for examinations should understand both the constitutional rules that govern the office and the historical milestones attached to individual leaders. A clear grasp of appointment, tenure and the Council of Ministers helps in answering questions on the Prime Minister's position in the Union Government. Modi's record is a reminder that the office rests on the confidence of the Lok Sabha, not just on the length of a term.

Price indices are widely used to track inflation, and the Wholesale Price Index (WPI) is a key measure among them. The Government of India has now approved a revision of the WPI base year, moving the reference point of the index to a more recent period. A base year is the reference period against which later price movements are measured, so changing it allows the index to reflect the structure of the modern economy more accurately. Economic activity has changed considerably since the earlier base year was fixed. The revision therefore aims to capture these shifts in the composition of goods, in the way they are classified and in the way their relative importance is measured. Accurate measurement matters because the WPI sits early in the supply chain, and its movements often signal pressures that may later reach consumers. Alongside the revised WPI, the Government has decided to introduce new Producer Price Indices. These indices are meant to give a wider picture of the prices that producers receive and pay, and of the costs they face in production. Together, the revised series is expected to provide a more complete view of inflation at the producer level, helping policymakers, businesses and analysts read cost and price dynamics with greater confidence.

The Quad is a grouping of India, the United States, Japan and Australia that has grown from a set of humanitarian contacts into a diplomatic grouping. Its roots lie in cooperation that followed a devastating disaster in the Indian Ocean region. A Japanese leader later gave the idea a sharper political shape, and the grouping was revitalised in response to growing unease about the expanding military and economic presence of a large regional power in the Indo-Pacific.

Today the Quad works as an informal strategic partnership rather than a formal alliance. Its stated aim is a region that is free, open, inclusive, secure and prosperous, anchored in the rule of law, freedom of navigation, territorial integrity and the peaceful resolution of disputes. These principles are applied in practice through specific initiatives, each with its own focus areas and objectives.

The eleventh foreign ministers' meeting of the group turned these ideas into concrete outcomes across several areas. Maritime cooperation is one strand, with shared surveillance tools and data arrangements focused initially on the Indian Ocean. Other outcomes cover critical minerals, energy, undersea connectivity, digital identity systems and agriculture. Many of these efforts aim to reduce dependence on a few suppliers and to build resilient supply chains and infrastructure across the region.

India's efforts to protect its green cover combine large national missions with focused local drives. The National Mission for Green India concentrates on expanding forest and tree cover while also improving the quality of the cover that already exists. Funds for compensatory afforestation are managed by a dedicated authority, which supports regeneration on degraded land. India also protects its wetlands, and several of these are recognised as Ramsar Sites. Two major programmes were started to protect large wild animals, one focused on tigers and another on elephants. Along the coastline, mangroves are being promoted through a national initiative that seeks to support both habitats and local livelihoods. The Aravalli Green Wall is a planned green belt along a mountain range. Public participation is also encouraged, and campaigns invite ordinary people to plant trees as part of the effort. India further publishes a periodic national report on the condition of its forests. Taken together, these measures show how planning, public funds, wildlife protection and citizen action work side by side to protect the natural environment.

Supporters of the June 2026 understanding argue that its benefits would reach well beyond the two signatories. A safer environment in the region could lower the likelihood of direct military clashes and of confrontations fought through allied groups. Calmer conditions would also make oil supplies more dependable, and lower crude prices could ease the financial strain on countries that import most of their energy. Shipping costs could fall as insurers judge a critical route to be less risky, and investment could flow back into areas hit by conflict, helping to rebuild them. New trade links could also connect the markets of West and Central Asia, and the reintegration of the country could give a north-south transport corridor a fresh boost. Yet the outlook is not uniform. Some analysts doubt that the parties can settle every disputed issue in the time allowed. Meanwhile, tensions involving regional proxies remain. Balancing these hopes against those risks will shape whether the accord delivers lasting dividends for the wider region.

The Draft Rules for the VB-G RAM G Act 2025 change how central money reaches states for rural employment. Under the earlier scheme, funding followed an open-ended, demand-driven model. Under the new approach, central allocations are set by a normative allocation formula. This formula is based on devolution criteria recommended by a finance commission and uses several weighted factors. One factor measures how far a state's per capita income lags behind that of the wealthiest states. Another reflects population and the employment demand that comes with it. The aim is to give economically weaker states a larger share and to promote equitable distribution.

Cost sharing is also revised. General States share costs with the Centre in one ratio, while Northeastern and Himalayan States receive a higher central share. Any expenditure beyond the approved normative allocation must be fully financed by the concerned state government. Central assistance is also linked to performance. From a later year of implementation, a portion of funds depends on timely wage payments, compliance with social audit requirements, completion of public works and overall implementation efficiency.

A National Level Steering Committee oversees these matters. It recommends state-wise allocations, formulates operational standards and monitors implementation and compliance.

Most discussion of inflation focuses on the prices that households pay, yet the prices that producers receive and pay also shape the economy. A manufacturer that receives lower prices for its output may reduce production, while a rise in the cost of materials or energy can squeeze profits and later feed into the prices of finished goods. Policymakers therefore need measures that show price movements from the producer's side of the chain. Economic activity today is also not limited to physical goods. The service sector is also part of economic activity, and a separate Service Producer Price Index tracks its prices. A measure that covers only goods can leave important producer-side changes out of view. To address such gaps, the Government has decided to introduce a new family of producer indices alongside the revised wholesale index. The indices are intended to capture price changes at different stages of production and across services as well. They are also expected to help analysts understand cost conditions and supply-side pressures faced by businesses. Because producers operate in many sectors, a broader set of indices allows a more detailed reading of how cost and revenue pressures move through the economy. Such information can help central planners, investors and industry bodies anticipate changes in inflation before they fully appear in consumer prices.

Economic security has become a central part of the Quad's agenda. Members have recognised that depending on a small number of suppliers for essential raw materials can create supply vulnerabilities, so they are working to spread sources more widely. Cooperation now spans the full life cycle of key minerals, from mining and processing to recycling, with the aim of making supply less exposed to shocks.

Energy is another priority. The group has agreed to a joint regional approach that links energy technology, supply chain strength and the assessment of market risks. This work is meant to help countries across the Indo-Pacific manage market risks.

The Pacific islands are also part of the agenda. A planned outreach effort aims to link island nations of the Pacific Islands Forum through a more robust network and to modernise ports, with completion targeted for the near term.

On technology, the Quad is developing practical tools for digital systems. Officials are preparing a reference document that will help public and private platforms work with one another across borders. A separate initiative uses artificial intelligence, robotics and remote sensing to support farming and food security. Together these efforts seek to make growth in the region both secure and resilient.

India's biofuel effort rests on several policy instruments. The National Policy on Biofuels aims to reduce import dependence by promoting blends of bioethanol, biodiesel and bio-CNG. One scheme provides financial assistance for second-generation ethanol made from surplus biomass and agricultural waste. Another scheme focuses on managing cattle dung and solid waste on farms and turning them into useful products. A separate policy aims to create bio-foundries that would produce biotechnology-developed feedstock and catalysts, and planned enzyme production would support existing and proposed ethanol plants in several states. India also joined partners to launch an alliance focused on sustainable biofuels and cooperation between countries. Another initiative aims to build an ecosystem that collects used cooking oil and converts it into biodiesel. The Cabinet has approved a hydrogen mission with targets for green hydrogen capacity, renewable energy capacity addition and jobs. Taken together, these measures show how biofuel policy spans agriculture, energy, waste management and international cooperation. Policy design in this area also looks at farm residue, since stubble and dung can be turned into fuel and compost. Several initiatives are run by different bodies, so the same raw material can fall under more than one programme.

facts.title: Why Telegram was blocked
facts.summary: MeitY temporarily blocked Telegram in India under Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000, after criminal groups allegedly used its message-editing feature to target candidates of the NEET-UG 2026 Re-Examination. Fraudsters edited old messages after an exam had ended to create a false appearance of a pre-exam leak. The booklet also links rising cybercrime complaints to activities organised within Telegram groups.
facts: MeitY temporarily blocked Telegram in India under Section 69A of the IT Act, 2000.
Criminal groups allegedly used message editing to target and defraud NEET-UG 2026 Re-Examination candidates.
Fraudsters inserted fake exam papers into old messages after an exam had ended.
This retroactive editing created a false appearance of a pre-exam leak.
Hidden phone numbers and end-to-end encryption in secret chats make tracing malicious actors nearly impossible for investigators.
Telegram hosts marketplaces for renting bank accounts used in money laundering, extortion and illegal gambling.
Criminals use automated bots to distribute illegal content and coordinate large-scale activities with minimal manual effort.
Government data shows a sharp rise in official cybercrime complaints linked to activities in Telegram groups.

facts.title: Maritime and Security Cooperation
facts.summary: Maritime cooperation is one strand of the 11th meeting's outcomes. The outcomes include a surveillance framework that uses tracking assets of all members and a partnership for near real-time maritime data. Security work also covers the Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission, the Malabar Exercise and a counterterrorism tabletop exercise.
facts: Indo-Pacific Maritime Surveillance Collaboration uses tracking and monitoring assets of all Quad members.
Immediate focus area of maritime surveillance: the Indian Ocean Region.
Maritime surveillance objective: strengthen maritime domain awareness and monitor illicit maritime activities.
Indo-Pacific Partnership for Maritime Domain Awareness enables near real-time maritime data sharing across regional waters.
Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission was launched under the Wilmington Declaration.
Quad-at-Sea objective: improve naval coordination, enhance interoperability, counter illegal maritime activities.
India will host the next edition of the Quad-at-Sea Ship Observer Mission.
Malabar Exercise is an annual multilateral naval exercise of Quad members.
Quad Counterterrorism Tabletop Exercise focuses on state-sponsored terrorism, UAV threats and joint crisis response planning; to be hosted by Australia in 2026.
